title: Memory Bandwidth, Not FLOPs: Profiling and Accelerating Query-Based Segmentation Decoders on Edge GPUs
abstract: arXiv:2610.22377v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Query-based segmentation models achieve strong performance even under real-time inference on workstation GPUs. On edge devices, however, we show their transformer decoders are deeply memory-bandwidth-bound, a bottleneck invisible to standard FLOP analysis that worsens with input resolution and limited DRAM bandwidth. An FP16 roofline analysis with tensor-core GEMMs active and hardware DRAM counters shows that the non-tensor-core aggregates of FastInst and Mask2Former reach only $2.5\%$ to $6\%$ of the CUDA-core ridge yet account for $53\%$ to $70\%$ of decoder time and $61\%$ to $71\%$ of decoder bytes. The largest individual kernels sustain up to $90\%$ of nominal peak DRAM bandwidth, effectively saturating the memory bus. The bottleneck is therefore not primarily low GEMM intensity, but cross-kernel activation traffic. translated_title: 内存带宽，而非FLOPs：在边缘GPU上剖析与加速基于查询的分割解码器
translated_abstract: 基于查询的分割模型即使在工作站GPU上进行实时推理时也能取得出色的性能。然而，我们发现在边缘设备上，其Transformer解码器严重受限于内存带宽——这一瓶颈在标准的FLOP分析中不可见，并且随着输入分辨率的提高和DRAM带宽的限制而加剧。通过启用张量核心GEMM的FP16屋顶线分析与硬件DRAM计数器测量表明，FastInst和Mask2Former的非张量核心部分仅达到CUDA核心脊点的2.5%至6%，却占用了解码器时间的53%至70%以及解码器字节数的61%至71%。其中最大的单个内核可持续维持高达90%的标称峰值DRAM带宽，实际上已使内存总线饱和。因此，瓶颈主要并非源于较低的GEMM计算强度，而在于跨内核的激活数据传输。CompactInst通过4倍的无参数空间池化来解决这一瓶颈，从而减少了传输的字节数（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该研究揭示了边缘GPU上基于查询的分割模型解码器的真正瓶颈是内存带宽（跨内核激活数据传输）而非FLOPs，并提出CompactInst，利用4倍无参数空间池化减少内存传输以实现加速。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that query-based segmentation decoders on edge GPUs are bottlenecked by memory bandwidth (cross-kernel activation traffic) rather than FLOPs, and proposes CompactInst, which employs 4× parameter-free spatial pooling to reduce memory traffic and accelerate inference.
